instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Get It on the Record
cards.instruction: Get formal approval, endorsement, or acknowledgment before anyone can quietly revise their position.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Initial the festival budget before lunch. I'll call this discussion finished when your yes is on the page.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I just said yes. Isn't that enough?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For you to begin initialing. You said yes to the fireworks last year too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And I changed my mind. Am I not allowed to?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You are. Date this yes first. Then any change comes back to me beside the position you're changing; we won't have two memories chairing the next meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I pay the builder, sign that my fence can stay on our boundary. I'll wait here while you choose your wording.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I suppose it can. Does that count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As the start. Write 'can stay' beside your name; I'll decide we're finished when the permission is clear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want to promise forever. Could we make it just today's agreement?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can. Write today's date. You keep a copy; I'll take mine to the builder. If you want to change it, bring your copy to me and we'll mark the change together.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Assigned by Procedure
cards.instruction: Get someone to accept an unwanted responsibility by proving that the rules, rotation, or tradition make it theirs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's your bin night. The rota puts you on Tuesdays; I'll hear any swap request before you go out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I took yours last week. Can't that cover tonight?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. I took your Thursday in return. This box says 'one week only'; you can check it before taking the bins.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You added that box. Since when do you decide the rules?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Since you asked me to write that one so I couldn't keep your easy Thursday. I'll uphold it for both of us. Your Thursday is safe; your Tuesday is waiting outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Congratulations on becoming club president. Here are the toilet keys.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought the caretaker cleaned them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. We voted to save that fee. The minutes assign closing and cleaning to the president.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I proposed that when you were president.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, and I cleaned them all year. Your first presidential duty is continuing your savings.

cards.title: Complete the Record
cards.instruction: Get someone to fill the missing gaps in an account without revealing which answer matters most to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm completing the party report. Give me arrivals, room changes and departures, in that order; I'll set the headings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You want to know who was near your cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may put refreshments in a separate section. Start with arrivals; nobody gets skipped because they didn't eat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ria left before the cake came out. She's standing here now; shall I send her home?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After her times are in. Bring her over; I'll take her account first, then yours. She gets the same three headings. You can both correct what I write, but neither account gets a special shortcut.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm completing the shared car log. Give me mileage, fuel and who drove after nine. I'll take them in that order.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You mean who dented it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can raise that once the row is complete. Start with mileage; the other columns aren't decoration.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Driver I remember. The rest means going down six flights to the glovebox.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll fetch the book. You stay here and put the kettle on; we'll do the whole row over tea. Take your time with the cups. I want the mileage as carefully remembered as anything else.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Make It Official
cards.instruction: Recruit someone by giving them a title, role, or ceremonial duty that makes participation feel binding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I've made you Keeper of the Festival Lantern.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only said I'd hold it while you tied your shoe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. An excellent probationary performance. Here's your badge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How long is the appointment?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Until you find a qualified successor. The lantern must never be abandoned.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Would you be honorary patron of our roof appeal? You'd open it and thank the donors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can come, but I won't make a speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then accept the patron's ribbon and lead the applause. That can be your ceremonial duty.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I leave after the first donation?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The patron applauds every donor. We couldn't have the later ones thinking their money mattered less.

cards.title: Request an Exception
cards.instruction: Get someone to bend one rule first so you can treat the decision as a precedent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll keep my bicycle inside the cafe for this shower. You can make one exception while I order.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only because it's raining. Don't put it by the tables.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The entrance will do. Write 'bicycle admitted in rain' in the shift book; I'll check the wording before I leave.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Jo's on tomorrow. She'll say this was only my decision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put your name beside it, then. A decision needs someone to have made it. I'll show Jo your entry if it rains again; you may add that I kept clear of the tables.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll bring my completed form tomorrow. You can give me one extra day as a trial.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody has had an extension. Why should I start with you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're welcome to start with me. Write today's deadline beside tomorrow's; I'll bring the form then and we can compare the damage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One day. No more. I'm marking it as an exception.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Date that note and keep it with the form when I bring it. Next time, bring this trial out before you tell anyone we've never allowed an extra day. We'll have an actual result to discuss.
